title: 2022 HMMT November Theme Problem 2
statement: Alice is thinking of a positive real number \(x\), and Bob is thinking of a positive real number \(y\). Given that \(x^{\sqrt{y}}=27\) and \((\sqrt{x})^{y}=9\), compute \(x y\).

solutions.text:
Note that

\[27^{\sqrt{y}}=\left(x^{\sqrt{y}}\right)^{\sqrt{y}}=x^{y}=(\sqrt{x})^{2 y}=81,\]

so \(\sqrt{y}=4 / 3\) or \(y=16 / 9\). It follows that \(x^{4 / 3}=27\) or \(x=9 \sqrt[4]{3}\). The final answer is \(9 \sqrt[4]{3} \cdot 16 / 9=16 \sqrt[4]{3}\).
